incidents.title: Search and filters Slowness

incidents.body:
**Root Cause**

The issue was caused by an automation process that affected the system's performance. During this time, the speed of processing tasks was slower than usual, impacting the overall efficiency.

**Resolution**

The problematic automation was removed, which restored the system's performance back to its normal state, ensuring that operations could continue smoothly.
incidents.title: Automations Slowness

incidents.body:
**Root Cause**

The issue was traced back to a firmware update in a database instance, which led to a failure in the system's ability to switch over to a backup. This caused the main application to go down.

**Resolution**

The problem was resolved by starting the database on a new healthy instance, restoring the system's functionality.

**Action Plan**

- To prevent future occurrences, a manual switch-over will be performed before any instance restarts. 
- Additionally, a maintenance is scheduled for the system update to address the identified bug.

The application experienced performance issues due to a spike in executing flows that affected the app's performance. During the investigation, an issue was identified, requiring a fix to resolve the problem permanently.

**Resolution**

**Action Plan**

The team will monitor new metrics in the scenario, to avoid the future impact

This incident has been resolved.

Today at 1:58 PM (UTC) our monitoring service identified a failure to communicate with the Redis database service responsible for background  jobs.

At 2:00 PM (UTC) our team decided to put our disaster recovery in action, creating a new database that was finished successfully at 14:10 (UTC).

Our automated test was run to check the overall status of the system. We've also put it online again for all users at 14:12 (UTC).

incidents.title: Major Incident detected

incidents.body:
We identify the problem, it happened because the gem [sequenced](https://github.com/derrickreimer/sequenced) that we use in our Ruby project locked the phase table, after that this process died and table stay locked.

We kill the process and restart the application that returns to respond as expected. Now we are removing that gem and move this logic to our database that can do this job in the same process and prevent this error.
